gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Chunky, bendy, hard to ignore. Plakkaat is best at shouting with its looped, nearly closed letters, while Noto Sans Siddham is best at quietly carrying text with its deep middle band and open s.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Plakkaat comes in heavy and bent like straw, its terminals curling back toward the stem. Noto Sans Sinhala holds the line with a dark stripe of lowercase and curve endings that keep their distance.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-sundane: Heavy, rounded and bold, Plakkaat leans on closed curves while Noto Sans Sundanese opens its e crossbars wide. Nudge the body size up a touch so those open shapes can breathe.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Friendly, though Plakkaat is plenty heavy. Its curves are as thick as its stems and nearly closed, while Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in every bowl, like an open rope bight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-syloti-: Plakkaat has a smooth, tube-like look, with every heavy line swelling out and its terminals curling back toward the stem. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri answers with short ascenders and a tall x-height.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Plakkaat is heavy and bent like straw, its curves nearly sealing shut at the ends. Yet Noto Sans Syriac stays open, with blown-glass bowls and an s that turns wide and easy.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Plakkaat is heavy, bent and bold. It does best when a title needs weight and closed curves, whereas Noto Sans Syriac Eastern is built for text, with tall lowercase against small caps.

Modern is the body's mood, and it contrasts sharply with the marker-tip heft of Plakkaat. Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke, so its dense little letters look like bundled cable.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Bent-straw lines and terminals that curl nearly back to the stem make Plakkaat instantly recognizable. Noto Sans Tagalog then fills the line with a dominant middle zone and generous gaps in its curves.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-tagbanw: Plakkaat looks like bent wire sign lettering, constant in thickness and heavy throughout. Noto Sans Tagbanwa takes the quieter job, with open curves and lowercase filling most of the height.
